goal: Deliver the specified categorized GitHub repository session experience with host-owned authentication/catalog, credential-safe server preparation, independent clones, repository-scoped devcontainers, accessible progress, exact-version migration, and fidelity-backed external seams.
approach: Use a fixed client-host OAuth App device-flow authority and retained complete catalog; route bounded one-use authority to authenticated servers; prepare repositories in a durable server aggregate; publish a Session only after durable clone, matching repository environment, and launch success; project the state through the existing host-neutral FleetRuntime and shared SPA. No third-party dependency is selected.

requirements.statement: The client host shall be the sole owner of GitHub OAuth transactions, bearer and refresh credentials, credential persistence, and refresh authority; it shall project no credential into the shared SPA, URL, web storage, catalog, fleet snapshot, diagnostic, or server durable state.

When GitHub account authorization or refresh completes, is denied, expires, is cancelled, or fails, the system shall expose that distinct account outcome, preserve the New Session query, all-source filter, and healthy project results, and return focus to the GitHub category entry.

While a GitHub catalog refresh is running or has failed, the client host shall retain the last validated complete catalog generation as stale and selectable, publish no partial generation, and leave the Projects source available.

The categorized target picker shall represent project and repository targets as a source-discriminated union and shall continuously expose project server identity or repository owner/name and source in visual, keyboard, pointer, and accessibility-tree observations.

When a repository is selected, the system shall preserve its immutable GitHub repository identity while execution server selection occurs afterward; back, cancel, refresh invalidation, and server invalidation shall preserve the query and every still-valid selection.

If an execution server lacks bearer authentication, exact protocol match, HTTPS, or loopback transport, then repository credential lease admission shall fail before token transfer, lease creation, preparation creation, or filesystem mutation with a typed server-scoped outcome.

The clone service shall derive the github.com HTTPS remote from validated owner/name and shall provide repository-bound authority only through a replay-resistant one-use broker; credentials shall never appear in remote URLs, argv, environment values, git config, files, persistence, or logs.
When two creation intents target the same repository, the server shall allocate distinct session identities and clone paths without duplicate blocking, automatic switching, or clone sharing.

When clone publication succeeds, the server shall publish clone-ready only after staging durability, atomic rename, parent-directory durability, and a matching immutable marker; conflicting or unsupported paths shall never be overwritten.

While repository preparation is incomplete, failed, cancelled, interrupted, or internally corrupt, the server shall keep it outside the available Sessions collection; one reducer transition may publish a Session only after validated clone, environment, and launch success.

When preparation is cancelled, retried, or abandoned, the server shall fence the observed revision, stop only owned work, retain clone-ready state for devcontainer retry, resume from the durable retry stage, and delete unpublished or never-available resources only after terminal abandon.

When the server restarts, it shall discard credential leases, normalize in-progress work to typed interrupted state, reconcile clone and environment durable evidence deterministically, and require fresh authority before resuming the same durable creation intent.

A repository devcontainer shall be keyed by execution-server-qualified immutable GitHub repository identity with per-project isolation; every session shall use an independent clone workspace while a matching ready repository environment is reused.

While preparation changes stage, the server domain snapshot and host FleetRuntime shall publish server-qualified stage, typed failure, retry origin, repository identity, server identity, environment disposition, and monotonic revision to every view; clone and devcontainer transitions shall be announced once through the existing polite live region.

When one catalog source, fleet member, repository, or execution server fails or becomes invalid, the picker shall update only that scope, preserve healthy sources and servers, query/filter and valid selections, and move focus to the scoped status action or next valid target.

While repository search-field validation is unresolved, matching shall use owner/name only; any known-target discovery or ambiguous-identification failure shall invalidate the assumption and reopen a follow-up decision without silently enabling extended metadata or changing topology/ranking.
At all times, no incomplete, failed, cancelled, interrupted, corrupt, or staging repository preparation shall be observable as an available Session.
At all times, GitHub authentication, catalog, refresh, credential, or repository preparation failure shall not reduce fleet-wide server project discovery or project-session creation availability.
At all times, repository, execution server, creation intent, preparation, session, clone path, and repository environment identities shall remain distinct and fully qualified end to end.

At all times, repository protocol surfaces shall admit success only under one exact protocol token shared by the daemon IPC, gateway REST/WS, SPA codec, Web/Workspace/Windows hosts, SDK transports, simulator, fixtures, and Playwright backend.

At all times, every GitHub auth/API, git, filesystem/process, and repository-devcontainer dependency shall have a reusable fake, a named invariant contract, and an opt-in FakeVsReal fidelity backstop; a mismatch shall be fixed in the fake rather than weakening the invariant.
At all times, GitHub bearer and refresh credentials shall be absent from browser-visible state, URLs, web storage, request diagnostics, argv, environment values, git config, and durable server state.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: Repository authority is admitted only through an authenticated exact-version HTTPS or loopback route; no-auth servers return authenticated_transport_required before side effects. A lease is repository-bound, one-use, memory-only, expires after 60 seconds, and each host may have at most 32 unconsumed leases.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Security contract tests exercise no-auth, mismatch, redirect, expiry, replay, revoke, and sentinel scans over all credential surfaces.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: One host runs at most one catalog authorization poll and one catalog refresh. Refresh uses 10-second request timeout, 120-second total deadline, 100 pages, 10,000 repositories, 32 MiB response bytes, and 16 MiB retained-cache bytes; a limit discards the unpublished generation as catalog_too_large or refresh_deadline.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Deterministic clock and paginated fake measure requests, elapsed deadline, item/page/byte counters, retained cache size, cancellation, and leak-free convergence.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: A server permits at most 4 active and 32 queued repository preparations, 2 active preparations per repository, one clone process/staging tree per intent, and 20 GiB of aggregate never-available clone data; capacity rejection occurs before filesystem mutation.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Repeated distinct-intent admission tests assert queue/process/staging/byte caps and 24-hour cleanup of terminal abandoned or orphaned never-available resources.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: Credential, catalog, preparation, clone, and environment records use same-filesystem temp write, file fsync/close, atomic rename, and parent-directory fsync where durability is claimed; unsupported publication fails closed.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Crash-point matrices cover every step before and after rename, directory fsync, record commit, and startup reconciliation.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: Target options alone occupy the grouped listbox; source status/auth/retry controls form an adjacent focusable control group. Stable-key aria-activedescendant, deterministic recovery, and one polite live region expose source and preparation transitions without nested interactive options.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Real-DOM accessibility tests and Playwright verify roles, names, focus order/recovery, and exactly one announcement for each stage transition lasting at least 500 ms; terminal outcomes announce immediately.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: User-visible diagnostics expose stable stage and a typed sanitized code only; raw OAuth bodies, request headers, unrestricted git stderr, and credential-bearing values are prohibited.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Sentinel and bounded-diagnostic tests scan host/server logs, errors, fixtures, process surfaces, git config, and durable records.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: The exact-version gate precedes lease or repository mutation, and all changed daemon IPC, REST/WS, host parser, SPA codec, SDK, simulator, fixture, and Playwright fake consumers migrate together.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Compile/round-trip/drift checks plus old-client/new-server and new-client/old-server no-side-effect matrices.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: Network, OAuth clock, random IDs, credential store, process runner, filesystem, preparation/environment store, and devcontainer manager are injected seams; hermetic T0/T1/T2 and opt-in T3 tests use the same named contracts.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: Test inventory maps each external dependency to fake, invariant contract, FakeVsReal test, fixture authority, and explicit skip condition.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: No new third-party dependency is selected; implementation uses Go and Node standard libraries plus dependencies already present in the repository.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: go.mod, package manifests, lockfiles, and imports show no newly selected dependency for this change.

adrs.title: Client-host GitHub device-flow account and catalog authority
adrs.context: Browser and Electron require one credential-safe account/catalog capability without callback or installation authority divergence.
adrs.decision: Pending consultation, use a GitHub OAuth App device flow with fixed public client_id and scopes. Each host owns protected credential persistence/refresh and a bounded validated complete-generation catalog, while the SPA receives only credential-free status, repositories, and a discriminated target projection.
consequences: One auth/catalog state machine can be conformance-tested across both hosts.
A dedicated OAuth App registration and controlled T3 account are operational prerequisites.
GitHub App installation administration, callback OAuth, ambient gh auth, and silent metadata expansion remain outside this change.

alternatives.why_not: Adds installation/admin and callback authority states not present in the UX.
Makes credential authority and availability host-environment dependent.

alternatives.option: Browser callback plus Electron custom protocol
alternatives.why_not: Creates two security and recovery state machines.

adrs.title: Ephemeral GitHub clone authority
adrs.context: A selected remote server needs private-repository authority without acquiring durable account ownership or exposing a token to renderer/process surfaces.
adrs.decision: Pending consultation, authenticated exact-version HTTPS or loopback admission creates a 60-second repository-bound one-use memory lease; no-auth servers reject it. A peer-credential and inherited-pipe-nonce-bound askpass broker consumes authority once and exposes only typed sanitized results.
consequences: Remote private clone can preserve client-host account ownership.
Servers without bearer authentication cannot create repository sessions.
The server maintains a bounded 32-entry per-host lease table and a platform askpass helper.

alternatives.option: Token in URL, argv, environment, or git config
alternatives.why_not: Leaks authority through durable or process-visible surfaces.
Creates a second ambient credential authority.
Changes git semantics and adds a large transfer/provenance boundary.

adrs.title: Durable repository preparation before Session publication
adrs.context: Clone and environment work outlive requests, may crash or be cancelled, and must not expose a partial Session or duplicate clone.
adrs.decision: Pending consultation, a host-persisted creation intent maps to a server-owned durable RepositoryPreparation. The reducer owns revision-fenced transitions, bounded admission, durable clone publication/reconciliation, retry/cancel/abandon, progress snapshots, and the only commit into an available Session.
consequences: Incomplete work is structurally excluded from Sessions and can resume after restart.
A new durable aggregate, capacity policy, reconciliation algorithm, and exact-version wire surface are required.
Completed session workspaces remain user data; only never-available resources receive automatic cleanup.

alternatives.option: Publish a partial Session before clone
Keep preparation only in an HTTP goroutine
alternatives.why_not: Cannot preserve retry identity or survive restart.

adrs.title: Repository-scoped devcontainer over session-specific clones
adrs.context: Current project path participates in both container key and workspace path, but approved UX requires one repository environment and independent session clones.
adrs.decision: Pending consultation, persist an execution-server-qualified repository environment record binding GitHub repository ID, container identity, pinned devcontainer digest/generation, and readiness. Mount the repository sessions root, use each session clone as frame cwd, and permit per-project isolation only.
consequences: Two sessions reuse one matching repository environment while keeping separate clones.
Environment recreation is explicit when durable and runtime evidence disagree.
Launch-plan and sandbox descriptors must separate environment scope from frame workspace.

alternatives.option: Use clone path as container key
alternatives.why_not: Silently creates one environment per session.
